scores.why: The only angle that answers "no goal" and "a reason to keep making and playing levels" directly. Three stars per room, a star only pays the first time (a new photo is worth about twice a replay), an album, quests and a daily photo. The film cans also fix part of "boring" from the player's side. board-canisters-1 shows them on photo surfaces away from the magenta ladder: two on the r17 bookcase top, one on the r25 cabinet top. 173 of 182 cans sit at least 2 cells off the ascent (median 6), and the rooms average 2.39 cans. So the player leaves the film stair to explore the photo even before the stair itself improves. G1 needs no record bump, so it can ship on v1. The mockup board fits 340 px, though the title is now six controls deep. Minus points: on r05 and r64 the cans sit on the wall-shading staircase, the star pay buys nothing until the Darkroom exists, and none of it has been played.

The only angle that measurably makes levels less filmy, and the boards show it. On board-r47 the route walks the desks, the whiteboard tray and the projector bar (81% film down to 20%). On board-model-10 it uses the bookcase shelves instead of a ladder up the right wall (93% down to 46% and 36%). On board-r03 vae crosses to the mirror top. Film drops 64.8% to 49.3% on the real photos and 73.3% to 54.8% on the model, the photo surfaces stood on go from 3.6 to 5.8, no room is lost and the bot clears every level. It is already sb-levels' planned v2 step. Minus points: board-model-41 is still a film diagonal on a bare wall (47% of climb rows have nothing in the photo to stand on), unused tabs stay on screen (r03), build cost is about 2x, and the real-photo numbers come from only 22 photos.

Answers "I really have to move the cropper around" and "it keeps telling me try a tighter crop". The pick built 27 of 28 photos against 21 for tonight's nearest search, and on board-r07 it builds where the search failed after 49 builds. Desert drops from 46% to 16%, and nothing changes in the record. But the gold-box levels still climb film: on board-r11 the tabs run up the right side, on m03 the pick is a film ladder up a well (worse than the search) and m04 is blank wall read as a slope. Film only drops from 60% to 51%, and the pick is a zoom into one object (median 0.56 of the default width). It is a better search, not a better level, and it trusts the bad reading.

Goes straight at "usually straight up" by changing the shape of the film. Seen on the boards: the switchback on alone-blank-wall-vZ, the zigzag crossing the room on r35, and the chimney on o13 is a good fit for that room. Stair moves fall from 41.8% to 19.9% in the rooms that get a piece, and the bot clears all 34. But film share is unchanged (60.8% against 61.1%): it is still floating platforms, just arranged. On board-r40 the gallery is as dense as the stair it replaces, and its lowest frame is drawn over the spawn; on r31 the frames overlap. The biome order was never exercised (the rooms are almost all Attic), and the chimney needs a new cell type.

It is the right diagnosis of the newest finding, and default-box builds go from 15 to 29 of 95 (median search builds 11 down to 3). But on its own the player sees worse levels. On board-img-scene-3 the new level is 12 film tabs straight up the right edge, on r18 the new level is a film diagonal, and r13 fails outright (it picked the beamed ceiling as the wall). Desert rises from 44.7% to 54.3% and film from 61.1% to 63.3%, and the QR grows from version 20 to 23. It only pays off underneath climb (furniture becomes something to stand on) and goals (cans move onto the real furniture). It also risks breaking climb's wallSet edge ledges.

On board-view-r01-0 the room becomes recognisable (window bars, frames), but the film ladder up the left edge is the same in all three panels, and r24 and r59 are the same. It does nothing for "boring" or "no goal", adds decoy shelf lines (p90 12 per level) and hides detail inside solids. The one valuable part is the grid coder: a median of 175 bytes against 582 raw, so the QR goes from version 20 to about 11. That is worth keeping only to make room for read's mask without growing the QR.

verdicts.plan:
TONIGHT (sb-m1-5, before the box stops at about 04:05 UTC):
1. sb-levels: build climb lane A (edge ledges, stepping stones, 8 passes, the whole-build fallback), gated on the record v2 that carries tonight's biome byte. This is already the lane's next step, and it is the largest measured drop in film. Make the bot clear the levels, add the V1_CHANGED and FALLBACK_LOST rows, and LOOK at r47, model-10 and scene-3 on the page before deploying.
2. In the same v2 header, reserve a flags byte now (bit 0 for a solid mask, bit 1 for a coded grid, bit 2 for detail). Then the reading and the coder can come later as flags and not as v3 and v4 decoders (look's version-sprawl risk).
3. If one lane frees up (after weapons step 2, with weapons step 3 pushed to tomorrow), build goals G1 film cans: the core-features film step, LOOT_FILM, a placeholder can, \"Film n/m\" in the strip, and the H-film tests. It needs no record bump, gives his phone something to hunt off the ladder tonight, and the cans go onto the new photo surfaces that climb lane A creates. Re-pin the goldens once. Order it after weapons step 2 so the two loot-list appends do not collide.

TOMORROW:
4. Goals G2: stars, album, quests deck v1 and the daily photo \"a room you have never climbed\", after sb-house merges (that lane owns the doorway card). Stephen rules on star pay against Q97 cosmetics.
5. Frame: the auto-frame scorer replaces the nearest search's choice, with the blank guard measured first and \"Another view\". Rerun its measure with climb lane A in, because its post score uses film share and the two were never measured together. Time it on the Pixel.

LATER (this week):
7. Read's figure-ground mask plus look's grid coder only (no detail layer), as flags on v2. The coder pays for the mask so the QR does not grow. First fix the wall pick (rows 8 to 40, refuse regions that mostly touch the top) and prototype interior ledges for bookcases. Re-measure with climb in, and check that climb's wallSet still finds the wall under the new reading.

verdicts.cut:
Not now:
- Look's detail layer (2x2, 4x4, dither, Scale2x). It makes the room prettier but the film ladder on every board stays the same, and it adds decoy shelf lines. Keep only its grid coder, as an enabler for the mask.
- Read on its own. Its boards show the levels get worse (scene-3 is 12 tabs up the right edge, desert rises to 54%), so never ship it except under climb.
- Blank's gallery as built. On r40 it is as dense as the stair it replaces and is drawn over the spawn, and on r31 the frames overlap. Also cut the spring, crumbling and moving tabs, and frames that hold tiny photo crops.
- Climb's chain planner, route score and zigzag variant. The angle measured them itself, and none beat the simple stone.
- From goals: colour or green quests before the v2 \"Reads as\" badge, any quest that gates play, a time star, and the 300-room album until the export size is checked (start smaller).
- Frame's size floor and the other box shapes (it measured that shape makes no difference).
- Running a fourth heavy lane in parallel on 2 cores. If G1 cannot fit tonight, it waits rather than crowding out climb lane A, the only change that measurably makes the level itself less straight-up film.

scores.why: This is the best value per line of code against his most repeated complaint ("floating platforms, usually straight up"). I read buildAt, repair, stair and settle in sb-levels 42fc8b19a. The change stays inside buildAt (the edge ledge pass after plat) and repair (a stone choice, and a pass cap raised from 4 to 8). Every hop still comes from SB.reach.tables, so each stair is a chain of graph edges by construction and the bot proof carries over. On v1 records opts.noClimb gives today's level bit for bit. Measured: film share 64.8% to 49.3% on real photos and 73.3% to 54.8% on the painted model, no room lost, and the bot cleared 32/32 and 17/17. I opened board-r47 and board-model-10: the route really does walk the desks and the shelf boards. Merge risk is low: no running lane edits repair, and sb-house adds only 3 lines to core-pipeline (the features.ramp call after settle). Costs: (1) build time is about 2.2x today. PIPELINE_BUDGET_MS 50 is declared in TUNING but no test enforces it. Worse, the whole-build fallback means a box that refuses under both rule sets costs about 3.2x, and in the seek search most boxes refuse (median 11 builds per photo), so the search gets slower even though no frame freezes. (2) The real-photo numbers come from a 22-photo subset. (3) wallSet depends on how the photo is read, so it will interact with any later mask. (4) Rule 4, clearing unused film, has not been measured. These keep it from a 9.

This is the cheapest fix for "it's too hard to actually get the level to be made" and "I really have to move the cropper around". It is capture side only: the record, levelHash and the v1 codes are untouched, and the core gains one read-only frameScore that shares readA with buildAt (H-frame-1 holds them equal). It cannot break a climb, because the final build always runs on the real downscale with fallbacks. Measured on 28 real photos: 27 build against 21 for tonight's nearest-box search, and desert falls from 45.7% to 16.2% on the same photos. It also stops at 4 builds or 16 tries, which offsets the build cost that climb adds. I opened board-r11: the search climbs the window on 6 film ledges and the pick climbs the rattan chair. Points off: (1) it rewrites the seek worker and crop screen in shell-capture and shell-ui, the code sb-levels finished hours ago and is still editing for the normalisation, so it has to run in that lane, one after the other, not in parallel; (2) it trusts the reading, so on the painted rooms m03 and m04 its picks got worse (a film well, then blank wall read as a slope), and the blank guard is unmeasured; (3) moving his box before he touches it needs his ruling (Q96 ruling 3 covers only a refusal); (4) Pixel time is unmeasured (430 ms in Node, about 350 boxes plus about 14 builds in the worker).

It answers "no real goal" and "a reason to keep making levels" better than anything else here: the stars pay only the first time, so a new photo is worth twice a replay, and the daily photo sends him out with the camera. But tonight's cost and conflict risk are the highest of the six. G1 appends features.film to the pipeline FIELDS, so levelHash moves on every fixture and every v1 code, and the goldens need a re-pin. It also appends LOOT_FILM to the core-sim loot list, while sb-weapons-2 has 137 changed lines in core-sim and sb-house has 14 there plus 83 in core-features. G2 needs sb-house's doorway card and its saveDefaults change in core-record (56 lines). The cans follow the current reading: board-canisters-1 shows cans on a wall-shading staircase (r05, r64) and against the frame edge. Dead pixels still buy nothing, and sb-house already delivers the house run, the boss and a cosmetic per clear tonight. Build it right after those two lanes merge, with one golden re-pin.

It fixes the root of the newest finding. I opened board-img-scene-3: the shaded lower wall opens up and only the cabinet and the sofa read solid. Default-box builds go 15 to 29 of 95, and the search's median build count falls from 11 to 3. Because the mask is stored, the floats stay at capture and the core only reads bits, so determinism holds. But on its own it raises desert rows (44.7% to 54.3%) and film share (61.1% to 63.3%). It is three lanes (the capture plus the oracle, record v2 with the mask, and the buildAt switch). The QR grows from version 20 to 23 unless it is coded. The wall pick fails on r13 (a beamed ceiling) and r04, and 21 of 95 photos fall back to v1. Interior ledges inside big solids are needed and not prototyped. sb-levels' normalisation, which went in today, covers part of the same ground for free. It is worth building, but after the record coder exists and once the wall pick is limited to rows 8 to 40, not tonight.

The engineering is sound: the detail layer never touches seedOf, levelHash or collision, and v1 codes keep their look pixel for pixel. The record coder alone is the useful part: a median of 183 bytes against 582 takes the QR from version 20 to about 11, and it creates the room that read's mask needs. I opened view-r01-0: at real size the 2x2 detail makes the room recognisable while the tabs still read. But it addresses nothing on his complaint list ("enough colors" is the biome, already ruled in Q97). It needs a new bit-exact range coder of about 80 lines in core-record (only ideal code lengths were measured, not a real coder). It adds decoy ledges (p90 of 12 a level). It changes buildStatic and drawShare in shell-render, where sb-weapons-2 has 409 changed lines. And the solid blend hides most of the furniture anyway. Keep the coder for later, together with read; the detail layer comes last.

Film share does not move (61.1% against 60.8%), because the pieces are film by design. It rewrites the same repair function as climb, so the two cannot be built in parallel, and its numbers are measured on top of today's repair, not on top of climb, which already takes away much of the desert it targets. I opened room-r40: the gallery is still a straight column up the right side, now drawn as frames, with the lowest frame body over the spawn. That is the old ladder in costume, not a new route. Build p95 rises from 91 to 137 ms. The chimney needs a new solid-film cell type that core-features, the renderer and level.piece in FIELDS all have to respect. 8 of 76 rooms need the second repair pass on the stair alone. The biome ordering is untested, because almost every real room is Attic until the biome byte lands. Revisit only the zigzag, after climb and read land, and measure again on top of them.

verdicts.plan:
I opened 8 boards myself (climb r47 and model-10, frame r11, read scene-3, blank r40, look view-r01-0, the goals can board); the rest are scored on the JSON. The rule behind the order: a record v2 code is frozen the moment a level built from it is shared, exactly as v1 is now. So every rule that changes a level has to ride the one version bump tonight, and capture-only work can follow at any time.

TONIGHT (sb-levels lane, one step after another; deploy sb-m1-5):
1. Finish the capture normalisation now in progress (cf6999ccf), then the early deploy sb-m1-4 as planned.
2. Record v2 in core-record: pack, unpack, validate, encode, parseCode. The header is v=2, w, h, mode, focal, a biome byte (0 = today's rule, 1 to 5 name the biome) and a RULES byte (1 = tonight's rules). The rules byte matters most: later level changes (clearing unused film, read's mask, blank pieces) become rules 2 and 3 inside the same v2 decoder, not a v3. An unknown rules value reads as 'newer'. Tests: v1 levelHash unchanged on every fixture, a v2 round trip, a v2 code read by an old parseCode reports 'newer'.
3. Climb lane A on v2 rules 1: the edge ledges in buildAt, the stepping stone in repair (8 passes, TAB_MAX and the 15% cap unchanged), and the build() wrapper that falls back to today's rules on a refusal. noClimb is set from rec.v < 2. Redwatch rows LEDGE_ON_WALL, STONE_BELOW_TOP, V1_CHANGED and FALLBACK_LOST. H-bot walks on the model fixtures and the real fixtures. Before the deploy, time it under flock in throttled Chrome. If the p95 is far over 50 ms, cap the passes at 6 and skip the fallback's second build inside the seek search: a box that refuses both is refused, and only Develop on his own box gets the fallback.
4. Gate: if climb A is not green by about 02:45 UTC, deploy sb-m1-5 without v2 at all (no v2 code leaves the box). Do not ship a v2 with the biome byte alone and edge ledges later.
sb-weapons-2 and sb-house keep their lanes untouched tonight. Nothing above touches core-sim, core-features or shell-render.

TOMORROW:
5. Frame, in the sb-levels lane on top of the merged seek and normalisation: frameScore (read only, H-frame-1 equal to stage A), frameBoxes, the summed-area grid, the blank guard (measure it first), and the final build on the real downscale. Ask Stephen about (a) auto-framing on open. Until he rules, ship (c): on a refusal, pick the best box instead of the nearest. The two levers have never been measured together (frame and climb), so measure that before the deploy.
6. Climb lane B, clearing unused film, as v2 rules 2 after a timing check (each lifted tab pair costs one reach graph).
7. After sb-weapons-2 and sb-house merge: goals G1 (film cans, one golden re-pin, gated on v2 so v1 codes keep their levelHash and their cans), then G2 (stars, album, quests deck v1) on sb-house's doorway card.

LATER:
8. Look's record coder (SB.gridcode), tested as a real coder within a few bytes of the ideal sizes.
9. Then read's figure-ground mask as a v2 flag, coded, so the QR stays at or under version 20. First limit the wall pick to rows 8 to 40 and refuse a region that mostly touches the top; interior ledges come with it.
10. Colour quests and colour daily prompts once v2 biome and the 'Reads as' readout exist.
11. Look's 2x2 detail layer under the 582-byte budget, with the decoy gate.
12. Blank's zigzag, re-measured on top of climb and read, if bare walls still climb straight up.
verdicts.cut:
1. Blank's chimney and its new solid-film cell type. Every downstream block (core-features, the renderer, FIELDS) would have to learn it, for 5% of standing cells.
2. Blank's spring, crumbling and moving tabs: a new sim launch and a retable, per-cell timer state, a reach graph that knows about time. None of it is worth it before the climb is right.
3. The gallery as it stands. Board r40 shows the same column up the side, drawn as frames, with a frame body over the spawn and frames as dense as the stair.
4. Climb's surface chain planner, its route score that charges film, and the ZIG zigzag. All measured, and none beat the simple stepping stone.
5. Read's option (c), storing the wall's colour field in the share code. Floats in the core put determinism at risk.
6. Read as a separate release, and any uncoded 144-byte mask that pushes the QR to version 23.
7. Look's 4x4, ordered dither and Scale2x variants. 24 of 95 rooms (4x4) and 94 of 95 (dithered) fit no QR, and Scale2x floods the room with decoy ledges.
8. A separate v3 for detail. It rides the v2 flags or does not ship.
9. Goals' time star (no honest par), colour quests before the readout (a lottery that repeats \"I try to do something green\"), and a 300-room album in the save. Cap it at about 60 rooms: the full album is about 300 KB in localStorage and the export string.
10. Frame's size floor and 'Another view' until his own photos have been looked at.
11. Any fourth parallel lane tonight. The 2-core box runs one browser at a time and the three running lanes already share it; frame and climb both have to go through the sb-levels lane, one after the other.

scores.why: This angle fits the game best. Edge ledges plus stepping stones make the climb go over his furniture, and the film tabs go back to what DESIGN 6.7 and section 2 say they are: help placed where the photo runs out, not the level itself. On the boards the change is real. On model-10 the route walks the bookcase's shelf boards and only the last third is film (93% film becomes 36 to 46%). On r47 it walks the desks, the whiteboard tray and the projector bar (81% becomes 20%). It is exactly the item Q97 left 'still to put to him', and sb-levels already has it as its next step. It is gated on record v2, v1 codes build bit for bit as today, the whole-build fallback means no room is lost, and the bot cleared 32/32 and 17/17. Rule 4 (lift tabs nobody stands on) matters for fit: a dead tab is help that helps nobody and blurs the 'film is help' reading. What it unlocks: film cans and stars land on real surfaces, and set pieces only fire where the desert is real. Limits: it needs a DESIGN 6.7 redline he has to rule on. Bare walls (model-41) stay a stair. Its wallSet depends on the reading, so it has to be re-keyed when read lands.

This fixes the defect behind the newest finding and behind 'it won't build'. I opened board-img-scene-3: today the shaded lower wall is a stair-stepped red mass that swallows the cabinet. The new reading makes exactly the cabinet and the sofa solid and leaves the wall and the window open. That is DESIGN 0's promise ('shelves and table edges become platforms') kept: furniture reads as the room and the wall reads as wall. Builds at the default box go 15 to 29 of 95, and the search's median drops from 11 builds to 3. It unlocks the rest: the frame scorer stops being fooled (frame m03 and m04 fail because of the reading), cans leave the shading staircase (the goals board shows r05 and r64), and edge ledges get a true wall colour. Fit costs: it redlines DESIGN 6.3 (Otsu) and 6.13 ('everything else is recomputed'), because the mask is stored. A 1 bit mask derived from the photo is not the photo, so the privacy pillar holds, but he should know a new field is stored. The QR grows from version 20 to 23 unless the grid is coded (see look). The wall picker fails on r13 (it chose the beamed ceiling) and r04, and the bookcase's shelves are lost inside one block. On its own it adds desert (44.7% to 54.3%), so it must never ship without climb.

This is the right answer to 'no real goal' and 'a reason to keep making levels', and it sits beside the house run (Q96 ruling 1) rather than competing with it. Three stars a room, cans on the photo's own surfaces away from the ladder, an album of grids (grids only, which extends DESIGN 12's recent rooms with no privacy cost), and quests that send him out with the camera. Cans off the ascent reward climbing his furniture, which is the core fantasy. Fit problems I would fix before building: (1) The name collides with the game's grammar. 'Film' already means help terrain (film tabs), and the placeholder can wears the film tab cream, which Q13 reserves for tabs, so a collectible would read as help. Rename it and recolour it. (2) The star road's frame styles cut across Q97 ruling 4 (cosmetics from house clears), so keep cosmetics on clears unless he rules otherwise. (3) Star pay is DP with no Darkroom to spend it in. (4) The mockup is generic web CSS, not Astra's pixel frame, and its album thumbnails are placeholders. (5) Until read lands, cans sit on shading staircases (r05, r64 on the board) and on the frame edge. Colour quests rightly wait for the v2 biome byte and a 'Reads as' badge, so green is never a lottery again. G2 must wait for sb-house to merge, because sb-house owns the doorway card.

Two parts with very different fit. The range-coded grid (582 bytes down to a median of 183, lossless, integer-only, levels untouched) is a pure enabler. It is what lets read's mask ride in the share code without pushing the QR past version 20, so it should shape tonight's v2 header even if it is built later. The 2x2 detail layer makes the room recognisable: I opened view-r01-0, and the window bars and frames read where today has faint squares. But it does not answer what he said. 'Pixelate more stuff' means more photos becoming levels, and this changes how a level looks, not whether it builds. It also weakens two promises. First, a 48x96 detail grid is still 16 colours, but it is four times more of his room in every share, so the privacy line in DESIGN 1 and 6.2 needs his explicit ruling and the share sheet must show it. Second, on view-o02-128 the shelf boards draw as pink lines across open space that look standable but are not. That breaks 'the player can always tell furniture from help', in the other direction. The solid blend still hides the sofa (r01) and the lettered box (r59). Version sprawl is a real risk: if detail ships as v3, that is three decoders to keep forever.

The pieces turn unavoidable film into something designed, which honours DESIGN 6.11's 'a blank wall still yields a short playable climb'. Tying them to biomes gives Q97 ruling 1's biome-from-colour a visible identity. The chimney on o13 is the best match of piece to room in any proposal: nine straight tabs become a wall-jump climb of the real wall strip. But the boards argue against the gallery and the zigzag on fit. On r40 eleven gallery frames are as dense as the stair was, and the lowest is drawn over the spawn. On r35 frames scatter over the bright window. The zigzag costs 51 tabs on a blank wall. Film share does not fall (61.1% becomes 60.8%), so the room reads as more help, not more room. The chimney needs a new 'solid film' cell, which blurs the clean rule that solids are furniture and film is help. It is only safe if it is always drawn as film and features never carve it. The 'frames hold tiny crops of his photo' art call cannot work as written, because the photo never persists and a shared code has no photo, so it could only use the grid. The biome order was barely exercised (almost every real room is Attic today). Right shape, wrong time: build it only where desert remains after read and climb.

Option (a), auto-framing his photo on open, goes against the spirit of Q96 ruling 3 and of Q181, which built the search to keep his framing first because it overrides what he framed. The boards show why. On r11 the pick is a sliver of a rattan chair at the photo's edge (a median of 0.56 of the default width, as low as 0.28), so the level becomes a zoom of one object, not his room. On m03 the pick is a tiny window corner with a worse film ladder (80% against 46%), because the scorer trusts today's reading. On m04 it frames a blank wall whose shading became a slope. The idea underneath is sound and fits: on a refusal, take the best box that builds rather than the nearest (option c). That fixes the shots3 finding I opened, where the search lifted the box to the blank top and laid five ledges up the left edge. It needs no record change. 'Another view' (up to 4 built framings) gives more levels per photo, which feeds goals. Its value depends on read landing first, and it needs a size floor so the room stays a room.

verdicts.plan:
TONIGHT (sb-m1-5, by about 04:05 UTC; the box fits about 5 to 6 lane steps):
1. sb-levels, record v2 header (already planned): the biome byte (Q97 ruling 1) plus a flags byte. A v2 client refuses any flag bit it does not know, as newer. The header leaves room for a coded grid flag, a mask flag and a detail flag. Then read's mask and look's codec land later as v2 flags, not as v3 and v4. This is a design decision made tonight that costs no build time, and it heads off look's version-sprawl risk.
2. sb-levels, climb lane A on v2: edge ledges, stepping stones (up to 8 passes) and the whole-build fallback. Redwatch rows: LEDGE_ON_WALL, STONE_BELOW_TOP, V1_CHANGED, FALLBACK_LOST. Bot clears every built level. Put the DESIGN 6.7 redline to him with it. This is the single change that most directly replaces 'floating platforms straight up' with 'I climbed my furniture'.
3. sb-house keeps the house run, ramp, clay boss and cosmetic per clear. That is his chosen answer to 'no goal' (Q96 ruling 1, Q97 rulings 2 to 4). Do not load goals onto it tonight.
4. sb-weapons-2 continues untouched.
Show him boards climb/board-model-10 and board-r47 with the deploy.

TOMORROW:
5. sb-levels, read lane on the v2 mask flag. First add the two wall-picker fixes the boards demand: choose the wall only from rows 8 to 40, and refuse a region that mostly touches the top (r13). Interior ledges inside big solids come with it, so the bookcase keeps its shelves. Re-key climb's wallSet to read's wall region when a mask is present. Ship only with climb on, never alone. Windows as a frame with an open sill (matches climb's sill use on model-9). Hold the floorSolid option.
6. sb-levels, look's grid codec only, on the same v2 coded-grid flag, so grid plus mask stays at QR version 20 or lower. Exact round-trip and v1-unchanged tests.
7. sb-levels, climb lane B: lift unused tabs (DEAD_TAB_KEPT), after a phone timing check against the 50 ms budget.
8. sb-house after it merges, goals G1 and G2 on the house's cards and title. Fixes first: a new name and a non-cream colour for the 'film cans' so tab cream stays help only (Q13); cosmetics stay on house clears per Q97 ruling 4 unless he rules for a star road; Astra briefed for the can and the album frame. Cans placed only on v2 levels' real surfaces once read lands.
9. Frame option (c) only: on a refusal, Develop takes the best scoring box that builds instead of the nearest, after read, with a size floor of about 0.45 of the default width and the blank guard. 'Another view' up to 4.

LATER:
10. Blank set pieces where measured desert remains after read, climb and lift: the chimney first (the o13 case, drawn as film, never carved by features), then the gallery with body clearance (spawn, window, other frames). Biome-tied once biome-from-colour has shipped and real rooms leave Attic.
11. Goals deck v2: colour quests and daily colour prompts, after the crop screen's 'Reads as' badge. The green quest stays optional and says where green is found.
12. Look's 2x2 detail layer, only after his explicit privacy ruling (more of his room in every share) and a decoy fix. Either clamp open-cell contrast, or let climb's edge ledges make detail shelves real, which needs his ruling because detail would then change the level. Also only after a solid-blend board.
13. Spring tab and the Darkroom, so DP and stars have something to buy.
verdicts.cut:
1. Frame option (a), auto-framing his photo on open, unasked. It overrides his framing against the spirit of Q96 ruling 3 and Q181. On the boards it picks slivers at the photo's edge (r11 chair, r20 loft post) that make a level a zoom of one object, and with today's reading it picks worse ladders (m03) and blank wall dressed as stairs (m04). Keep only the scorer for refusals (option c).
2. The zigzag switchback: 51 tabs on a blank wall, which makes help the level and pushes rooms into the fallback.
3. Gallery frames that 'hold tiny crops of his photo': the photo never persists, and a shared code has no photo. If frames get art at all, it comes from the grid.
4. Climb's chain planner, route score and ZIG zigzag: measured, none beat the simple stone.
5. Look's Scale2x and outlines (38 decoy ledges per level), 4x4 detail and ordered dither (no QR for 1 room in 4, and 94 of 95 rooms respectively), and any detail budget above 582 bytes.
6. Read's floorSolid rule for now (it raises desert), and shipping read without climb (desert 44.7% becomes 54.3%, and he still sees film straight up).
7. The goals star road's frame styles, unless he rules for them, because cosmetics come from house clears (Q97 ruling 4). Also cut the time star (no honest par) and the 'film' name and cream colour for the collectible, which collide with film tabs and break 'the player can always tell furniture from help'.
8. Any record v3. Everything new rides v2 flags designed tonight.

plan.summary:
1. Today: the bug stands on film tabs 61.1% of the climb on 95 real photos (73.3% on the painted rooms), 44.7% of climb rows have nothing in the photo to stand on, and Attic is 44 of 47 rooms. The root cause, seen on the boards: a wall's own shading reads as solid, so the furniture disappears, the search drifts to the blank top of the room and the repair stacks tabs up the edge.
2. "Move the cropper around" is already being fixed tonight (the normalisation, then the search reaching every box that builds, target 94 of 95). This plan is about what the level is once it builds, and why you would shoot the next room.
3. Judges' totals: climb 24, goals 21, frame 18.5, read 17, blank 13.5, look 13. All three put climb first.
4. TONIGHT (sb-levels, one step after another, into sb-m1-5): record v2 with your biome byte, plus a rules byte and a flags byte so later level changes ride v2 and never need a v3. Then climb: edge ledges, stepping stones aimed at the photo's own tops, and a fallback so no room is lost. Measured: film 64.8% to 49.3% on real photos and 73.3% to 54.8% on the painted rooms, surfaces stood on 3.6 to 5.8, no room lost, the bot clears every level.
5. The gate: if the climb is not green by about 02:45 UTC, the biome ships alone (rules 0) and the climb follows tomorrow. It costs about 2.2 times today's build time, so it gets timed in a throttled browser before the deploy.
6. TOMORROW: when your box refuses, pick the best box instead of the nearest (frame option c: desert 45.7% to 16.2%); clear away film nobody stands on; snapshots, which are up to 3 finds a room placed on your furniture, 173 of 182 off the ladder (new branch sb-goals); three stars, an album and photo quests on the house branch.
7. LATER THIS WEEK: a coded share code (582 bytes down to a median of 183), then the figure and ground reading as a stored mask, only together with climb (default box builds 15 to 29 of 95, though alone it makes levels worse). Then colour quests after a "Reads as" badge, and chimney or switchback pieces only where bare walls are still left.
8. Not building: blank's gallery as it stands, spring, crumbling and moving tabs, look's 4x4 and dither, a time star, any record v3, and a fourth lane tonight on this 2 core box.
9. Honest limits: nothing here has been played on your phone. The climb's real photo numbers come from 22 photos. Bare walls (board model 41) still climb film until the new reading lands. No two levers have been measured together yet, so each lane measures that first.
10. You decide four things: what goes in tonight's v2, how far the auto framing goes, what stars pay, and whether the new reading comes this week.

questions.question: What should tonight's share code version 2 (deploy sb-m1-5) carry besides the biome byte you already ruled for? It will also carry a rules byte, so whatever is left out can follow later without breaking a shared code.

options.label: Biome plus the climb rules (Recommended)
options.description: Edge ledges and stepping stones aimed at the photo's own tops, 8 repair passes, and a fallback to today's rules so no room is lost. Film share of the climb falls from 64.8% to 49.3% on real photos, surfaces stood on go from 3.6 to 5.8, and the bot clears every level. Costs about 2.2 times today's build time and a DESIGN 6.7 redline. If it is not green by 02:45 UTC, the biome ships alone and the climb follows tomorrow.

options.label: Biome only tonight
options.description: Climb follows tomorrow after a phone timing check. Tonight's levels stay as filmy as today's.

options.label: Hold version 2 entirely
options.description: Wait until the climb and the new photo reading are both ready. The biome from colour waits too, so rooms stay mostly Attic for now.

questions.question: How far should the game go in choosing the crop box for you? Today, when Develop refuses your box, it moves to the nearest box that builds. A scorer that ranks a few hundred boxes by how climbable the photo is cut the empty stretches of climb from 45.7% to 16.2% on 28 real photos, though it tends to pick a small slice of the photo.

options.label: Only when your box refuses (Recommended)
options.description: Develop on a box that refuses takes the best scoring box that builds instead of the nearest. Your framing and your drag always come first. No record change.

options.label: Frame every photo on open
options.description: The box glides to the best part as soon as you pick a photo, and you can drag it back. More levels build without touching anything, but the game reframes your photo before you do.

options.label: A Find the best part button
options.description: The box stays where you put it until you tap the button.

options.label: Keep the nearest box search
options.description: No change. The search keeps drifting toward blank wall on busy photos.

questions.question: Each room is getting three stars (light the beacon, find every snapshot, take no hit), kept in an album, with photo quests. A star counts only the first time, so a new photo is worth about twice a replay. What should a star pay?

options.label: 5 Dead pixels, cosmetics stay on house clears (Recommended)
options.description: Each new star pays 5 Dead pixels the first time, in every mode. Frame styles and hero skins keep coming only from house clears, as your Q97 ruling 4 says. Dead pixels buy nothing until the Darkroom exists.

options.label: Also a star road of frame styles
options.description: 10, 25, 50 and 100 stars each unlock a frame style. A visible reward now, but it bends Q97 ruling 4, which ties frames to house clears.

options.label: Nothing but the album and quests
options.description: Stars only fill the album and finish quests. Nothing to spend.

questions.question: Should new photos be read by figure and ground? The game would find the wall from its own colour and shading, and a cell would be solid only where the photo differs from that wall, so a shaded wall stops swallowing the furniture. Default box builds go from 15 to 29 of 95 real photos, and the search needs a median of 3 builds instead of 11. On its own it makes levels emptier (desert 44.7% to 54.3%), and a 1 bit mask of the room is stored in the share code (not the photo).

options.label: This week, coded, only with the climb (Recommended)
options.description: After a smaller share code lands (582 bytes down to a median of 183), so the QR stays at version 20 or smaller. It ships only together with the climb rules, after the wall pick fix (no beamed ceilings) and shelf ledges inside big solids.

options.label: Not yet
options.description: Keep today's light and dark reading and revisit it once your own room photos have been measured.

briefs.lane: BIOME-V2: the biome from the photo's real colour, in a record v2 that can grow
briefs.brief: THE BIOME FROM THE PHOTO'S REAL COLOUR, IN A RECORD V2 THAT CAN GROW (Q97 ruling 1; the investigation's option B1 with the Frost rule first; the design sprint's plan /home/codespace/sb-drafts/design-nov01/PROPOSAL.md section 3 step 1). At capture, vote the biome from the averaged cell colours (after the normalisation, before quantizing) by hue band, with the bright room rule first. Carry it in a record v2 whose header is v=2, w, h, mode, focal, then three new bytes: BIOME (0 = derive it by today's rule, 1 to 5 = the biome), RULES (0 = today's level rules exactly; 1 is reserved for the climb rules, which the next step builds; any value this client does not know reads as 'newer'), FLAGS (all zero in this step; bit 0 coded grid, bit 1 solid mask and bit 2 detail are reserved for later lanes; any set bit this client does not know reads as 'newer'). Capture writes RULES 0 in this step. The seed still hashes only the grid. v1 codes and every fixture decode to the same levels (they keep biomeOf), and an old client refuses a v2 code with decode's existing why 'newer'. Read the prototype (hue bands and gates) in /home/codespace/sb-drafts/sameness/colour/analyze.js and its numbers in docs/SAMENESS-INVESTIGATION-OCT31.md, then build it properly in core-record (pack, unpack, validate, encode, parseCode), core-pipeline (the biome read from the record when set) and shell-capture, with the capture oracle taking the same vote. Tests: harness (v1 records and every fixture unchanged, levelHash pinned; a v2 record carries biome, rules and flags through encode, decode and build; a v2 record with RULES 0 builds the same level as the same grid in v1, the biome aside; parseCode answers 'newer' on RULES 9 and on an unknown flag bit; the hue vote on known colours: sage, mint and forest green to Overgrowth, navy and teal to Deep, blush and red to Ember, a white room to Frost, beige and wood to Attic), the capture gate (a green walled painted room develops as Overgrowth with its enemy kind), the share round trip. Redwatch rows: BIOME_IGNORED (the byte written but the build derives it), RULES_UNKNOWN_ACCEPTED, FLAGS_UNKNOWN_ACCEPTED, V1_CHANGED. Measure the biome spread before and after over the 120 room model (tools/room-model.js) and the real photo corpus (bash tools/run.sh in /home/codespace/sb-drafts/realphotos; today Attic 44 of 47 rooms). Shots of the develop reveal of a green, a navy and a pink room at 412x915, LOOKED at. Record: a PROGRESS entry headed BIOME, a State row, the next free QUESTIONS entry with the header layout and the DESIGN 6.10 and 6.13 redlines.

briefs.lane: CLIMB-A: edge ledges, stepping stones and the whole build fallback on v2 rules 1
briefs.brief: CLIMB THE PHOTO, LANE A (Q97 'still to put to him'; the design sprint's climb angle, /home/codespace/sb-drafts/design-nov01/climb/proposal.md, and PROPOSAL.md section 3 step 2). Read the working prototype first: /home/codespace/sb-drafts/design-nov01/climb/make.js (edge ledges and stones) and make2.js (the fallback and the noClimb gate), which patch the sb-levels page into vaef.html; build only what vaef has, not the chain planner, the route score or the zigzag (measured, none beat the stone). Everything runs only when rec.v >= 2 and rec.rules >= 1 (opts.noClimb otherwise, so v1 codes and RULES 0 codes build today's level bit for bit). (1) Edge ledges, in buildAt after solid and plat, before landmarks: wallSet = the two most common palette indices among open cells in rows 1 to h-2; a vertical pair (ia above, ib below) is an edge when neither is solid, ib is not wall paint, the indices differ, and luminance differs by more than 30, or S1000 by more than 350, or both have hue bands and the bands differ; a horizontal run of edges at least PLATFORM_RUN_MIN long becomes photo one ways on the lower row. (2) Stepping stones, in repair: each pass while the exit is unreached aims its stair at the unreached standable cell above the highest reached row, not standing on a tab, nearest by Chebyshev distance to any reached standable cell, ties to the lowest index; with no stone the pass does what today's does. REPAIR_PASSES 8 on these records (4 on the others); TAB_MAX 12 and REPAIR_MAX_CHANGE 0.15 unchanged; every hop still from SB.reach.tables. (3) build() runs the climb rules and, on a refusal, reruns today's rules on the same record and keeps that level (repair.wholeFallback = 1). Capture writes RULES 1 once this lands. Note that the prototype was measured on raw capture: measure again on the normalised capture. Tests: harness (a v1 fixture and a RULES 0 fixture build byte identical to today, levelHash pinned; every model room and real fixture that builds today still builds; an edge ledge never sits on wall paint; a stone is always above the highest reached row), H-bot walks that clear every built level on the model fixtures and on real photo fixtures (the prototype cleared 32 of 32 and 17 of 17). Redwatch rows: LEDGE_ON_WALL, STONE_BELOW_TOP, V1_CHANGED, FALLBACK_LOST. Measure before and after with tools/room-model.js and the FULL real corpus (all 95, bash tools/run.sh in /home/codespace/sb-drafts/realphotos; the prototype used 22): builds kept, film share of the ascent's standing cells (64.8% to 49.3% on 22 real photos, 73.3% to 54.8% on the model), rows on film, photo surfaces stood on, tabs per room, and the search's builds per photo. Time it under flock in throttled Chrome over the fixtures (p50 and p95 against PIPELINE_BUDGET_MS 50; vaef was 2.2x today in Node). If the p95 is far over, cap the passes at 6 and skip the fallback's second build inside the seek search (only Develop on the player's own box keeps it), and record that. Shots at 412x915 of the PLAYED level on the page for r47, model-10 and scene-3, plus the worst angle on purpose, model-41 (a bare wall), LOOKED at with three things wrong in each. Record: a PROGRESS entry headed CLIMB, a State row, the next free QUESTIONS entry with the DESIGN 6.7 redline (8 passes, the aimed stair, edge ledges as photo ledges, the fallback in place of 'ask for a tighter crop'). DEADLINE: if this is not green by about 02:45 UTC, leave capture writing RULES 0, commit what you have as work in progress, and tell the lead not to merge it for sb-m1-5.

briefs.lane: FRAME-C: on a refusal, the best scoring box that builds instead of the nearest
briefs.brief: PICK THE BEST BOX, NOT THE NEAREST (the design sprint's frame angle, option c only, /home/codespace/sb-drafts/design-nov01/frame/proposal.md; Q96 ruling 3 and Q181 stay true: his framing first, the search only after Develop refuses his box; unless he rules for auto framing on open, build no glide on open). Prototype: /home/codespace/sb-drafts/design-nov01/frame/run2.js and lib.js. Build: C.frameBoxes(bw, bh) (1:2 boxes from fit.w shrinking by 0.7744 a step to the 192 px minimum, positions every quarter box, clamped, no repeats, his box excluded as the seek does today); a summed area grid from the decoded photo, byte equal to the capture oracle's area average after the normalisation; SB.pipeline.frameScore(pal), read only, sharing readA with buildAt so they cannot drift; the cheap score Q from the proposal's rule 2; builds in Q order skipping any box with IoU over 0.6 against a refused one, stopping at 4 built or 16 tried, inside the seek worker's SLICE_MS slices; the pick by post score (1 minus desert share, minus 0.5 times the ascent's film share, plus 0.2 times min(1, climb/40)), which uses film share and so must run with the climb rules on; the blank guard (never a box with 3 or fewer palette entries over 2% of cells unless nothing else builds), measured first on the model and real picks; the final build always on the real C.downscale of the chosen box, falling back to the next pick and then to today's nearest search. Measure a size floor at none and at 0.45 of the default width, look at boards of both, and choose by what reads as the room; record why. Tests: H-frame-1 (frameScore equals stage A on every fixture and 60 model boxes), H-frame-2 (box order deterministic, clamped 1:2, no repeats), H-frame-3 (the grid byte equal to the oracle), H-frame-4 (the pick builds on all 60 model rooms and the final build runs on the real downscale), the capture gate (a refusing box ends on the best pick; a drag during the search keeps his box). Redwatch rows: FRAME_READ_DRIFT, FRAME_ORDER, FRAME_SAT_EQ, FRAME_BUILDS, FRAME_BLANK, FRAME_KEEPS_DRAG. Measure on the 95 real photos and tools/room-model.js against tonight's search (SEARCHR) and with the climb rules in: builds, desert rows, film share, builds per photo, Node time, and throttled Chrome time under flock. Shots of the crop screen at 412x915 and 360x780 for r11, r07 and m03 (the shaded painted room, the worst angle), LOOKED at. Record: a PROGRESS entry headed FRAMEC, a State row, the next free QUESTIONS entry.

briefs.lane: CLIMB-B: clear away film nobody stands on, as v2 rules 2
briefs.brief: CLEAR AWAY UNUSED FILM (the climb angle's rule 4; PROPOSAL.md section 3 step 4). Only after a timing check: time CLIMB-A on the phone profile first (throttled Chrome under flock, p95 against 50 ms), because each lifted tab pair costs one reach graph. After repair settles the route, lift each film tab pair the main ascent does not stand on, one at a time, keeping it lifted only if the exit stays reached, the reach share stays at or above REPAIR_REACH_FRAC and the main ascent's route score still passes; order by index so it is deterministic. Runs only on rec.rules >= 2; capture writes RULES 2 when this lands (tomorrow's deploy carries rules 2 together with the snapshots on sb-goals, which gate on the same value: the lead merges both before stamping). RULES 0 and 1 codes and every v1 code build exactly as before. Tests: harness (a built rules 2 level keeps no tab the ascent does not stand on unless lifting it breaks the route; rules 1 fixtures unchanged, levelHash pinned), H-bot clears every rules 2 level on the model and real fixtures. Redwatch rows: DEAD_TAB_KEPT, RULES1_CHANGED. Measure tabs per room, film share and build time before and after on tools/room-model.js and the real corpus. Shots of r03 and model-44 (the boards that showed unused tabs) at 412x915, LOOKED at. Record: a PROGRESS entry headed CLIMBB, a State row, the next free QUESTIONS entry.

briefs.lane: SNAPSHOTS (goals G1): up to 3 finds a room on the photo's own surfaces
briefs.branch: sb-goals (new, from add-sproing-jumper after sb-m1-5 merges)
briefs.brief: SNAPSHOTS, THE FINDS (the design sprint's goals angle, lane G1, /home/codespace/sb-drafts/design-nov01/goals/proposal.md, renamed per the design judge: never called film and never in the film tab cream, which means help under Q13; working name snapshots). Place them in core-features as the last step after settle, with no rng draw, only on rec.rules >= 2 (so every v1 code and every code shared on sb-m1-5 keeps its level; rooms without them show 'No snapshots in this room'). A spot is a standable cell reached from spawn whose cell below is photo (a one way that is not a film tab, or a solid above the floor row), at most spawn row minus 2, and not the spawn, exit, chest, scroll, door, a speck, an enemy cell or a pocket cell; a surface is a maximal run of spots in one row and its cell is the run's middle (left middle when even), preferring a cell not in column 0 or 23; off = the least Chebyshev distance to a standing node of the main ascent; sort by off (largest first), row (higher first), index; take a surface at least FILM_ROW_GAP 6 rows from every one taken; stop at CAP 3. Store as level.features.snap, appended to the level FIELDS. In core-sim append LOOT_SNAP after LOOT_BLUEPRINT (rebase on the merged weapons loot list first): touching one takes it like a speck, draws nothing and pays nothing, no new state field. In shell-render an 8x8 placeholder with a coloured border (not cream) until Astra draws one, and 'Snapshots 2/3' in the strip. Tests: H-snap-1 (every pick a reached photo spot, rows 6 apart, at most 3, in sort order), H-snap-2 (with snapshots stripped every fixture hashes as before and the rng stream is untouched; rules 0 and 1 records place none), H-snap-3 (the sim takes one, draws nothing, banks nothing). Redwatch rows: SNAP_ON_TAB, SNAP_UNREACHED, SNAP_GAP, SNAP_DRAWS, SNAP_MOVES_LEVEL, SNAP_ON_OLD_RULES. Goldens moved once through --regold --why. Measure on the real corpus and the model: snapshots per room, distance off the ascent (the prototype: mean 2.39 a room, 173 of 182 at least 2 cells off, median 6), and how many sit on photo furniture now that climb's edge ledges exist. Shots at 412x915 of r17, r25 and r05 (the worst angle: shading staircase) with the snapshots and the strip, LOOKED at. An Astra brief line for the snapshot sprite. Record: a PROGRESS entry headed SNAPS, a State row, QUESTIONS entries from Q220 (this branch's range is Q220 to Q239).

briefs.lane: STARS (goals G2): three stars a room, the album, photo quests deck 1, the daily photo
briefs.brief: STARS, ALBUM AND PHOTO QUESTS (the goals angle's lane G2; PROPOSAL.md section 3 step 6; build after the house lane B and SNAPSHOTS have merged, because this lane owns the doorway card and the title and reads the snapshot count). Stars per room: Beacon (the clear), Snapshots (every one taken, or the room has none), Clean (no EV.HURT from entry to the clear; a hit Thick Skin absorbs does not count). Best stars kept per grid seed; each new star pays as he rules in the star pay question (default STAR_DP 5 at x1 in every mode; cosmetics stay on house clears per Q97 ruling 4 unless he picks the star road). No time star. Album in the save: each cleared room as {code, seed, biome, stars bits, snaps [got, of], first date, clears}, newest first, capped at 60, seeded from recent rooms with the Beacon star only; fillSave adds it to old saves without a version bump; check the Settings export length. Screens: the star row on the clear card and the doorway; an album contact sheet 'Album 31 rooms, 64 stars' with five biome badges (the dim badge outlined, not plain grey); the quests list with 'Ready to collect'; on the title after the first clear, one line each for Today's photo, Album and Photo quests without pushing Free play below a 48 px target. Quests deck 1 in fixed order: Climb a new room 10, Find all the snapshots in a room 15, Three stars in a new room 25, Climb three new rooms in a day 30, Find all the snapshots in three rooms, Not a scratch in room 4 or 5 of a house 40, Clear a house with 10 stars or more. Daily photo: FNV-1a of the local date string over the prompt list, which before the Reads as badge holds only 'A room you have never climbed' (20 DP, a streak). No colour quests in this lane. Copy short enough not to wrap at 340 wide ('Lit the beacon', 'Snapshots 2 of 3', 'Not a scratch'). Tests: the save shape and the cap, the star rules (a hurt, Thick Skin, a room with no snapshots), star pay only the first time, the deck order, the daily pick by date. Redwatch rows: STAR_TWICE, STAR_HURT, ALBUM_CAP, DAILY_DATE, QUEST_ORDER. Shots at 412x915 and 360x780 of the title, the clear card, the doorway and the album, LOOKED at with three things wrong each. Record: a PROGRESS entry headed STARS, a State row, the next free QUESTIONS entry in Q200 to Q219.

briefs.lane: GRIDCODE: the coded share code grid as v2 flag bit 0
briefs.brief: A SMALLER SHARE CODE (the look angle's coder only, /home/codespace/sb-drafts/design-nov01/look/proposal.md rules 1 and 2; no detail layer). SB.gridcode in core-record, ES5 and integers only: each cell's colour as its rank in a candidate list (left, up, up left, up right without repeats, then 0..14 not yet listed) through an adaptive frequency range coder (15 symbols, counts from 1, +24 a use, halved past 65536), one table per context (distinct colours among left and up, and whether left equals up). Written when FLAGS bit 0 is set; capture sets it on new codes; v1 and uncoded v2 codes decode as before. Tests: exact round trip on every fixture and on the 95 real photo grids; the same record always gives the same bytes; real coded sizes within a few bytes of the measured ideal (median 175 bytes for the grid against 582); every fixture's coded v2 record 582 bytes or less; an old client answers 'newer' on the flag. Redwatch rows: CODEC_LOSSY, CODEC_NONDETERMINISTIC, V1_CHANGED. Measure link length and QR version through SB.qr over the corpus (expected about version 11). Shot of the share drawer's QR at 412x915, LOOKED at. Record: a PROGRESS entry headed GRIDCODE, a State row, the next free QUESTIONS entry.

briefs.lane: FIGURE: the figure and ground reading as a stored v2 mask, only with the climb rules
briefs.brief: READ THE PHOTO BY FIGURE AND GROUND (the read angle, /home/codespace/sb-drafts/design-nov01/read/proposal.md; only if he rules yes; only after GRIDCODE and CLIMB-A). At capture, on the full resolution crop after the normalisation: figure(crop) from the prototype fig.js (Lab at 96x192, texture, wall regions, the quadratic colour field, solid where the cell departs by more than 11 or texture over 9, bright low hue openings kept open, a smooth top region open above row 16, specks under 3 cells flipped), with the two fixes the boards demand: the wall chosen only from rows 8 to 40, refusing a region that mostly touches the top (r13), and ledges inside big solids so a bookcase keeps its shelves (prototype them first and show a board). No floor rule for now. Store the mask (FLAGS bit 1, coded with SB.gridcode so grid plus mask keeps the QR at version 20 or smaller) and give it the next RULES value; buildAt starts solid from the mask when both are present, and everything after is unchanged. Re key climb's wallSet to the figure's wall region when a mask is present, so edge ledges do not switch off. 21 of 95 real photos find no wall: they write no mask and keep today's reading. The capture oracle and test/capture.mjs take the same step. Tests: H-cap rows on painted fixtures (a shaded wall reads open, a cabinet solid, a window a frame with an open middle, a beamed ceiling never the wall, no wall gives no mask), v1 and earlier rules unchanged with levelHash pinned, a v2 mask deterministic through the core. Redwatch rows: WALL_PICK_TOP, FIELD_FIT_OFF, OPENING_SOLID, MASK_IGNORED, WALLSET_LOST, V1_CHANGED. Measure on the 95 real photos and the model WITH the climb rules: default box builds (15 to 29 alone), builds per search, desert, film share; it may ship only if film share is no worse than climb alone. Shots at 412x915 of scene-3, r18, r13 and r17, LOOKED at. Record: a PROGRESS entry headed FIGURE, a State row, the next free QUESTIONS entry with the DESIGN 6.3 and 6.13 redlines and the privacy note (a 1 bit mask derived from the photo is stored, never the photo).
